title: Signed relative Cartier Kummer boundary and its module realization
statement:
Fix $k,\ell,E,n\geq1,A=A_{E,n}$ as in [def-pur-conventions], and the twist of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $i:D\hookrightarrow T$ an effective Cartier divisor [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle], with $W=T\setminus D$. Put $N=\ell^n$, $R=\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z$ and $M=\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{N,T}$, with the exact Kummer sequence of [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. Use the relative cohomology and torsor-with-section classification of [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology]. Let $L=\mathcal I_D^\vee$, let $s_D$ be the section dual to $\mathcal I_D\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_T$, and let $P_D=\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}(\mathcal O_T,L)$ be its frame torsor [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor]. Set
$$\alpha_D=[P_D,s_D|_W]\in H^1(T,W;\mathbf G_m),\qquad \beta_D=\delta_{T,W}(\alpha_D)\in H^2(T,W;M).$$
Here $N$ is invertible on $T$ and $NA=0$. Form both relative derived section cones, for $R_T$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and for underlying abelian sheaves, of restriction from $T$ to $W$. The canonical comparison obtained by deriving coefficient forgetting is an isomorphism between these cones in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. It commutes with their maps to absolute derived sections and with the signed supported realization of [lem-pur-divisor-relative-cone], whose model has differential $D(a,b)=(da,r(a)-db)$ and kernel map $k\mapsto(k,0)$. Consequently $\beta_D$ has a canonical realization
$$b_D:i_*R_D\longrightarrow M[2]$$
in $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ via [lem-amb-closed-support-hom]; its underlying relative class is exactly $\beta_D$, with that sign and specified trivialization. Let $\nu:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and put $t=\sigma_T\rho_T:\nu^{-1}M\to A(1)_T$ using exactly the roots-projection coefficient map of [def-pur-frame-class]. For the general Cartier class of [lem-pur-divisor-class],
$$\operatorname{cl}(D)=t_*\nu^*\beta_D\quad\text{in }H_D^2(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A(1)),$$
where $\nu^*\beta_D$ is read through the same signed relative-to-supported comparison. This is an identity of the global relative classes, including their lift and trivialization, rather than just of their local restrictions or their images after forgetting support. No smoothness of $T$ or $D$ is required.

proof.text: Retain the existing cartierPoleBoundary with its specified complementary frame and define beta by composing it with the Kummer extension. The existing cartierReducedEtale is the uniquely normalized scalar adjunct, and reducedEtale_boundary of [lem-sp-cartier-reduction-site-comparison] proves SupportedKummerBoundary for both R=ULift(Z/(ell^n)) and A. Positivity, invertibility and coefficient annihilation are the unchanged PurityFiniteSetting constructions. No new choice of relative lift is made.

Apply exact scalar forgetting to the nonnegative module resolution and its augmentation. InjectiveResolution.descOfQuasiIso lifts the identity to the abelian injective resolution J; its augmentation identity and quasi-isomorphism instance give q. For each etale object V, [lem-sbc-injective-module-forget-evaluation-acyclic] says each forgotten injective module term is evaluation-acyclic, while the terms of J are evaluation-acyclic by injectivity. The nonnegative version of [lem-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity-quasi-iso], followed by extension by zero, makes both evaluated chain maps quasi-isomorphisms. Applying the mapping-cone triangle and the two-out-of-three lemma for a morphism of distinguished triangles makes the actual shifted cone map a quasi-isomorphism. The two cone-map encodings agree on both summand inclusions.

For module restriction surjectivity, exact sheafification makes an injective module sheaf injective as a presheaf. Use free R-modules on universe-lifted representables. Monicity of W to T makes their induced map monic; injectivity extends the morphism representing any section on W, giving its lift on T. Abelian restriction surjectivity is [lem-weil-pbc-injective-sheaf-mono-restriction]. Extend by zero, including negative degrees, and apply [lem-weil-degreewise-epi-kernel-cocone-qis] to both restriction maps. The resulting maps have exactly CartierKernelNormalization. Use kernel.map for the kernel comparison; its inclusion equation and both cone-coordinate equations prove the strict kernel square. The projection and boundary squares are triangleSquare from [lem-pur-divisor-relative-cone]. Two identity-augmented lifts are homotopic by CochainComplex.homotopyOfQuasiIso. The sectionMap_homotopy construction of [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] and Q_map_eq_of_homotopy give equality in the derived category.

The residue root map is invertible by [lem-sp-residue-finite-root-map-iso]. For either coefficient ring, the defining property of cartierReducedEtale supplied by [lem-sp-cartier-reduction-site-comparison] is its full supported scalar boundary equation. Unfold CartierEtaleReductionSpec and cartierEtaleKummerUnit, then reassociate Yoneda composition to obtain exactly beta followed by the specified ordinaryFiniteRootMap. This is an equality on supported Ext, retaining the sign and complement section.

The chosen generalDivisorEtaleClasses satisfies DivisorEtaleNormalized by its defining existsUnique_generalDivisorEtaleClasses theorem [lem-pur-divisor-class]. reducedEtale_eq_of_boundary of [lem-sp-cartier-reduction-site-comparison] identifies its Ext class with cartierRelativeCoefficientBoundary. The realizes field identifies its Hom representative with Ext.hom. Apply the unchanged functorialCupCompare, which is the definition of generalDivisorClass. This uses the general Cartier family and does not assume smoothness.

lean.note: Uses the existing normalized supported integral Ext model of the relative torsor class, including its specified complement section. The finite R-root line is the canonical tensor-with-R chart; the theorem states that its actual root map is invertible. The full cone comparison is an isomorphism in D(Ab), with the actual localized diagonal map, projection, boundary, normalized kernel inclusions and their square. No smoothness, coefficient flatness or ramification-divisibility restriction is added.
